18	
19	# 论文写作风格规范
20	
21	> 核心哲学：**论文是一个有说服力的故事，不是实验报告。** 审稿人在几十秒内判断论文价值——如果 Abstract 和 Introduction 读起来像实验日志，论文就已经失败了。
22	
23	---
24	
25	## 一、总体写作哲学
26	
27	### 1.1 故事驱动，不是数据堆砌
28	
29	- 论文必须以"故事线"为核心展开：问题 → 洞察 → 方法 → 验证
30	- 禁止大量实验数据堆砌——每个数字出现必须服务于叙事推进
31	- 附录内容必须在正文中有明确引用且融入叙事，禁止简单堆砌
32	- 如果附录数据对核心叙事有重大影响，根据附录数据调整论文 framing
33	
34	### 1.2 主线统一性
35	
36	- 当 idea 在研究过程中发生变化后，**必须重审全文逻辑**
37	- 常见问题：Introduction 讲的故事 A，Method 做的是故事 B，Results 又在讲故事 C
38	- 修复方式：从最终实验结论反推，重写 Introduction 的问题定义和动机
39	- 每次 idea 调整后检查：Abstract → Introduction → Method → Results → Discussion → Conclusion 是否形成一条连贯主线
40	
41	### 1.3 专有名词必须有定义
42	
43	- 首次出现的专有名词/缩写必须给出完整定义和解释
44	- Abstract 中使用的缩写也必须在 Abstract 内定义（如 LLM = Large Language Model）
45	- 不能假设读者知道你自己定义的术语——论文从来没解释过的概念不能直接使用
46	- 通用规则：如果一个非标准术语第一次出现时没有括号定义，就是写作 bug
47	
48	### 1.4 写作前必读同类优秀论文
49	
50	- 每个章节动笔前，找 **2-3 篇目标会议近 1-2 年的高分论文**作为风格参考——同类问题或同类方法皆可
51	- 重点学：
52	  - Abstract 怎么用最少篇幅讲完故事
53	  - Introduction 怎么从大问题切入到具体贡献
54	  - Related Work 怎么 positioning 自己（不是 survey）
55	  - Table/Figure 怎么压缩信息密度
56	- **不是抄袭**，是学习同行的故事节奏和审美——不同子领域叙事节奏差异很大
57	- 实操：Paper Agent 可以从 `literature_map.yaml` 中挑 `role=foundation` 或 `role=direct-competitor` 的论文，把 `{title, venue, year, abstract}` 附在 Worker 的 task_prompt 中作为概念参考；如需学习写作风格本身，让 Worker 通过 WebSearch 取得论文链接并 fetch 全文
58	
59	---
60	
61	## 二、Abstract 写作规范
62	
63	### 2.1 四个必答问题（150-250 words）
64	
65	Abstract 必须在很短的篇幅内清楚回答：
66	1. **研究什么问题** — 1-2 句话交代背景和痛点
67	2. **为什么重要** — 现有方法的不足（不用写太多）
68	3. **本文提出什么** — 核心贡献的关键机制（简要，不堆砌细节）
69	4. **结果说明什么** — 用具体实验结论支撑贡献
70	
71	### 2.2 禁忌
72	
73	- **禁止堆砌数据**：Abstract 不是 Results 的缩写。最多引用 2-3 个关键数字，要服务于 claim
74	- **

tool_args.old_string:
\textit{Derivation.} Three mutually exclusive cases determine gradient direction for a window with locally correct actions: (1)~episode succeeded (probability $p$): correct sign; (2)~episode failed but group contains a success (probability $(1{-}p)[1{-}(1{-}p)^{K-1}]$): wrong sign; (3)~entire group failed (probability $(1{-}p)^K$): zero gradient. Conditioning on non-zero gradient (Cases 1 and 2) yields Equation~\ref{eq:correct_conditional}.

At $p{=}12.5\%$, $K{=}8$, only 19.1\% of gradient updates have the correct sign (Figure~\ref{fig:theory_curve}). In the large-$K$ limit, $P(\text{correct} \mid \text{update}) \to p$: ${\sim}87.5\%$ of updates for locally correct windows point in the wrong direction.
tool_args.new_string:
\textit{Derivation.} Three mutually exclusive cases determine gradient direction for a window with locally correct actions: (1)~episode succeeded (probability $p$): correct sign; (2)~episode failed but group contains a success (probability $(1{-}p)[1{-}(1{-}p)^{K-1}]$): wrong sign; (3)~entire group failed (probability $(1{-}p)^K$): zero gradient. Conditioning on non-zero gradient (Cases 1 and 2) yields Equation~\ref{eq:correct_conditional}. The bound is tight when episode success implies all constituent windows are locally correct; in practice, successful episodes may contain suboptimal windows, so the true fraction of correctly signed updates may be lower.

At $p{=}12.5\%$, $K{=}8$, this yields an upper bound of 19.1\% on correctly signed gradient updates (Figure~\ref{fig:theory_curve}). In the large-$K$ limit, $P(\text{correct} \mid \text{update}) \to p$: ${\sim}87.5\%$ of updates for locally correct windows point in the wrong direction.

tool_args.new_string: We evaluate on ALFWorld~\cite{shridhar2021alfworld}, a text-based household environment with six task types requiring sequential reasoning over up to 50 steps. Our theoretical analysis (Section~\ref{sec:theory}) assumes the simplified binary case ($R \in \{0, r_+\}$), which yields an upper bound on sign misattribution severity; Section~\ref{sec:sign_verification} validates this bound under both reward structures. The base policy is Qwen3-1.7B fine-tuned on expert demonstrations (SFT baseline: 12.5\% in-distribution). At this baseline success rate, Proposition~2 predicts the majority of gradient updates carry incorrect sign. All conditions use RAGEN~\cite{ragen2025} (v0.1, commit \texttt{3a6b48b})\footnote{Our implementation extends RAGEN v0.1 with episode-level training support. Code available upon acceptance.} with GRPO~\cite{shao2024deepseekmath} ($K{=}8$; full hyperparameters in Appendix~\ref{app:hyperparameters}). We report success rate on a 134-task OOD set (primary) and 32-task in-distribution set (secondary). Seed counts are noted per condition.

tool_args.new_string:
\subsection{Sign Misattribution Verification}
\label{sec:sign_verification}

We distinguish three metrics that each capture a different aspect of credit assignment quality:

\textit{(1) Sign-episode correlation}: whether advantage sign tracks episode outcome (success/failure). Under pure binary reward (penalty${=}0$), this correlation is 100\% ($n{=}157$ windows; Figure~\ref{fig:sign_misattribution}), directly confirming M2: advantage sign is entirely determined by episode outcome, not local action quality. This is by construction, since all windows in a successful episode share the same positive return under binary reward.% exp_id: binary_credit_agreement_iter0

\textit{(2) Credit agreement rate}: whether advantage sign matches local action quality, operationalized through action validity as a proxy for local correctness (Definition~1). Under step-independent training with penalty reward ($h{=}2$, $n{=}3{,}000$ windows), only 52.07\% of windows with valid actions receive positive advantage, marginally above random chance ($p{=}0.025$ vs.\ 50\%; $+$2.07pp effect size). This near-random credit agreement shows that advantage sign carries almost no information about local action quality. Penalty reward partially breaks sign-episode correlation by introducing within-group variance, but the resulting signal remains too weak for meaningful credit assignment. This operationalization is conservative: successful episodes may contain suboptimal windows, making our validity label an upper bound on true local correctness. Even under this generous criterion, credit agreement remains near-random, strengthening the diagnosis.% exp_id: 7b_cell_a_h2

\textit{(3) $P(\text{correct} \mid \text{update})$}: the theoretical upper bound from Proposition~2 ($\leq$19.1\% at $p{=}12.5\%$, $K{=}8$). This bounds the fraction of non-zero gradient updates with correct sign, a different quantity from the credit agreement rate, which conditions on action validity rather than gradient participation. The two metrics are complementary: Proposition~2 bounds worst-case gradient quality; credit agreement measures empirical signal strength.

Combined with $\gamma{=}1.0$ collapse (Appendix~\ref{app:additional}), these measurements confirm sign misattribution as the causal driver of training failure.
